The current bug report suggests that there is an issue with the behavior of `CommandLine.getOptionValue(String opt)`. The user expects to retrieve the option value using a specific key but finds that they need to use a different key instead.

From the provided failing test code, the test creates an option with a short name 'd' and a long name 'debug'. It then parses the command line with this option and tries to retrieve the option value using the long name 'debugOpt', which results in `null`.

Looking at the implementation of `CommandLine.getOptionValue(String opt)`, it internally calls `getOptionValues(opt)` and returns the first value in the array. If the option values array is `null`, it returns `null`.

The issue likely occurs because the `getOptionValue` method expects the option key used during parsing, which is the short name 'd' in this case, instead of the long name 'debugOpt'.

To fix this issue, the user should use the short name 'd' to retrieve the option value instead of the long name 'debugOpt'.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLine.getOptionValue(String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
